# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 7 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 18

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 2: "pleasure of sleep" — marital context

- **EMET:** "the pleasure of sleep that goes with marriage"
- **LOGOS:** "the pleasure that accompanies sleep in marriage"
- **PNEUMA:** "the pleasure that belongs to sleep and marriage"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — most natural English word order; all agents correctly identify hēdonēn hypnou as the marital pleasure of conjugal rest.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 3: "kindred earth" vs. "earth that suffers all alike"

- **EMET:** "earth that suffers all alike" (homotimou gēs)
- **LOGOS:** "kindred earth"
- **PNEUMA:** "the same earth that receives us all"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "kindred earth" — homotimos means "of equal honor/value"; the earth is "kindred" in that it holds equal relation to all humanity; EMET's "suffers all alike" is a free expansion; PNEUMA's "receives us all" is acceptable but too funerary.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 6: "one entrance into life" vs. "one way into life"

- **EMET:** "one entrance into life, and a common departure"
- **LOGOS:** "one way into life for all, and one way out"
- **PNEUMA:** "one door in for all of us, and one door out"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "one way into life for all, and one way out" — eisodos (entrance/way in) and exodos (way out) are preserved as a pair; PNEUMA's "door" is vivid but introduces a spatial metaphor not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 7: "spirit of wisdom came to me" vs. "spirit of wisdom came"

- **EMET:** "the spirit of wisdom came to me"
- **LOGOS:** "the spirit of wisdom came to me"
- **PNEUMA:** "the spirit of wisdom came" (omits "to me")
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "came to me" — PNEUMA's omission weakens the personal reception; the Greek epēlthen ep' eme explicitly includes the dative "to me."

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 9: "priceless gem" vs. "precious stone"

- **EMET:** "any priceless gem"
- **LOGOS:** "any precious stone"
- **PNEUMA:** "any precious stone"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "precious stone" — lithon polutelē means a costly stone; "priceless" (EMET) is a paraphrase; "precious stone" is standard and accurate.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 10: "radiance never ceases" vs. "shining is unquenchable"

- **EMET:** "her radiance never ceases"
- **LOGOS:** "her shining is unquenchable"
- **PNEUMA:** "her light never goes out"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "her shining is unquenchable" — ou sbennytai means "is not quenched/extinguished"; "unquenchable" is the precise word; EMET's "never ceases" is too gentle; PNEUMA's "goes out" is acceptable but informal.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 12: "she was their mother"

- **EMET:** "though I did not know that she was their mother"
- **LOGOS:** "but I did not know then that she was the mother of them all"
- **PNEUMA:** "What I didn't know yet was that she was the mother of it all"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — "the mother of them all" gives the full rhetorical emphasis; "then" clarifies temporal sequence; PNEUMA's "it all" is slightly less personal.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 13: "without guile" vs. "unselfishly"

- **EMET:** "What I learned without guile I share without envy"
- **LOGOS:** "What I learned unselfishly I share unsparingly"
- **PNEUMA:** "I learned without holding anything back. I share without holding anything back."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — adolōs (without guile/deceit) in the sharing context means freely/without holding back; "unselfishly" best captures the ethical quality; PNEUMA's double repetition is effective orally but redundant in text.

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 14: "unfailing treasure" vs. "inexhaustible treasure"

- **EMET:** "an unfailing treasure for men"
- **LOGOS:** "an inexhaustible treasure for human beings"
- **PNEUMA:** "an inexhaustible treasure for all human beings"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "inexhaustible treasure for human beings" — anekleipton thēsauron means a treasure that cannot be emptied; "inexhaustible" is more precise than "unfailing."

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 15: "corrector of the wise" vs. "keeps the wise on course"

- **EMET:** "the corrector of the wise" (katorthōtēs)
- **LOGOS:** "the one who keeps the wise on course"
- **PNEUMA:** "keeps the wise from going wrong"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "the one who keeps the wise on course" — katorthōtēs means one who makes things go straight/right; EMET's "corrector" implies prior error; LOGOS's rendering captures the guiding function without that implication.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 20: "virtues of roots" vs. "healing properties of roots"

- **EMET:** "the virtues of roots"
- **LOGOS:** "the healing properties of roots"
- **PNEUMA:** "the medicinal properties of roots"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "healing properties of roots" — dunameōn rhizōn in this encyclopedic context refers to medicinal properties; "virtues" is archaic; LOGOS and PNEUMA are both correct; SOPHIA prefers LOGOS as "healing" is slightly warmer.

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 21: "fashioner of all things" vs. "designer of all things"

- **EMET:** "wisdom, the fashioner of all things"
- **LOGOS:** "wisdom, the designer of all things"
- **PNEUMA:** "wisdom, the maker of everything"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "designer of all things" — technitis means a craftsperson/artisan with skill and design; "designer" captures both the skill and the intentionality; "fashioner" (EMET) is acceptable; "maker" (PNEUMA) is too broad.

---

## Disagreement 13 — Verse 22: "manifold" vs. "many-faceted" — polumerēs

- **EMET:** "manifold" (polumerēs)
- **LOGOS:** "manifold"
- **PNEUMA:** "many-faceted"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "manifold" — polumerēs means "of many parts/aspects"; "manifold" is the standard English theological rendering; "many-faceted" (PNEUMA) is vivid but modern.

---

## Disagreement 14 — Verse 22: "clear" vs. "lucid" — trancherēs

- **EMET:** "clear"
- **LOGOS:** "lucid"
- **PNEUMA:** "lucid"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "lucid" — trancherēs means transparent/clear; "lucid" in the sense of clarity of light and mind is more elevated for this register.

---

## Disagreement 15 — Verse 25: "emanation" vs. "outflowing" — aporroia

- **EMET:** "a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty"
- **LOGOS:** "a pure outflowing of the glory of the Almighty"
- **PNEUMA:** "a pure stream flowing out from the glory of the Almighty"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "pure outflowing" (LOGOS) — aporroia is a Stoic technical term meaning something that flows out/emanates from its source; "outflowing" is both precise and accessible; "emanation" (EMET) is traditional but philosophically loaded with later Gnostic connotations; PNEUMA's "stream" adds a water metaphor not in the Greek.

---

## Disagreement 16 — Verse 26: apaugasma — "reflection" vs. "radiance" vs. "brightness"

- **EMET:** "a reflection of eternal light"
- **LOGOS:** "a reflection of the eternal light"
- **PNEUMA:** "a radiance from the light that is eternal"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "a reflection of the eternal light" — apaugasma means the reflected gleam/radiance that shines back from a light source; "reflection" correctly preserves the secondary/relational nature; "radiance" (PNEUMA) makes Wisdom the source of light rather than its reflection, which is theologically distinct and incorrect here. Note: this same word (apaugasma) is used in Hebrews 1:3 of Christ.

---

## Disagreement 17 — Verse 27: "remains in herself" vs. "remaining within herself"

- **EMET:** "while remaining in herself, she renews all things"
- **LOGOS:** "remaining within herself, she renews everything"
- **PNEUMA:** "She stays entirely herself — yet she makes everything new"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — "remaining within herself" preserves the Platonic philosophical point: Wisdom is not depleted or altered by her activity; PNEUMA's rendering is vivid but "entirely herself" shifts the sense to identity rather than transcendence.

---

## Disagreement 18 — Verse 30: "evil does not prevail" vs. "evil never prevails"

- **EMET:** "against wisdom evil does not prevail"
- **LOGOS:** "against wisdom evil never prevails"
- **PNEUMA:** "nothing in existence overpowers wisdom"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "against wisdom evil never prevails" (LOGOS) — the "never" makes the universal claim explicit; kakotēs is specifically "wickedness/evil," not "nothing"; PNEUMA loses the specific adversarial relationship between evil and wisdom.
